question: Morning stiffness lasting more than 60 minutes that improves with activity is characteristic of inflammatory arthritis, whereas degenerative arthritis typically causes stiffness that worsens with use and lasts less than 30 minutes.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is true. The duration of morning stiffness is a cardinal distinguishing feature — >60 minutes strongly favours an inflammatory aetiology, whereas degenerative (osteoarthritic) stiffness is typically brief (<30 min) and worsens rather than improves with activity.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The duration and behaviour of morning stiffness is the key diagnostic pivot: inflammatory arthritis produces prolonged stiffness (>60 min) that loosens with movement due to synovial inflammation, while osteoarthritis produces brief gel-phenomenon stiffness (<30 min) that worsens with loading.
